correctness.rationale: For each integer d>=1 and all D,R>0, the unreset moment boundary-value problem yields three exact radial polynomials. The Poisson-renewal survival identity is differentiated at zero, yielding exact mean and variance sensitivities. The variance sign polynomial is strictly decreasing on [0,1], positive at 0 and negative at the previously known mean critical squared radius; hence the conflict shell is nonempty, unique and sharp. The algebra also proves the exact three-dimensional root and large-d law. The shipped standalone checker passed 97 symbolic identities, root/sign assertions and independently evaluated high-precision Laplace-transform tests. No numerical sample is used to prove an infinite quantifier.

originality.rationale: The accepted statement is the all-dimensional variance sensitivity and its strict separation from the established mean-benefit boundary, rather than the preexisting full Brownian exit/renewal transform. value.rationale: Variance and mean of an absorption time are separately natural engineering/search objectives. The theorem identifies a nonempty, sharply calculated physical shell in every dimension where weak resetting reduces variability only by sacrificing average speed; it also proves the reverse tradeoff is absent at first order and gives a simple exact three-dimensional boundary. A finite but all-dimensional complete threshold classification is more than a normalization check or known mean-only result. Its relevance does not require a separate downstream theorem. No global finite-rate optimum is claimed.
